To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the packaging of microsystems must be designed for the application; 2) the design process must be integrated with manufacturing and reliability; 3) the design must be driven by the system level requirements, not by the technology; 4) a systems approach must be taken; and 5) packaging must be a team effort.

the packaging of integrated systems is an enabling technology, that the packaging must provide high performance and low cost, that the packaging of the system must be designed to meet the requirements of the system, and that the packaging must be designed with manufacturability and reliability in mind.
Packaging design is critical to the success of integrated microsystems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of high-performance microsystem packaging technologies that are cost effective and manufacturable.
the packaging of high-performance, high-density, high-reliability, low-cost, intelligent, integrated microsystem products.
the development of a high-performance, low-cost packaging technology for integrated microsystems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single, best packaging solution.

the microsystem packaging technology is still in its infancy and will continue to develop rapidly in the coming years, and that the packaging of microsystems is a very complex and difficult problem that requires the concerted effort of many disciplines.
the microsystem packaging industry is in the process of a major transition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the packaging of integrated systems is an area that will require a significant effort in terms of technology development, design and manufacturing process optimization, and system integration.
we have developed a packaging technology that is capable of providing the necessary performance for the second silicon revolution.

the key to high performance packaging for microsystems will be the development of a system design approach, which integrates all aspects of packaging, from materials, through processes, to the final system performance.

packaging will have a profound impact on the success of the second silicon revolution.
packaging must be designed with a systems-level perspective.
the packaging of microsystems is a complex, multidisciplinary problem that will require a concerted effort from many different disciplines to achieve success.
